name: Can a fourplex be built as a prefab or modular project?

mainEntity.name: Is modular or prefab construction a good option for a fourplex in Los Angeles?
mainEntity.text: Is modular or prefab construction a good option for a fourplex in Los Angeles?

acceptedAnswer.text: This is a strong gap topic because many owners are looking for faster or more cost-predictable ways to build. Modular construction can reduce some onsite labor and shorten the active construction phase, but it adds complexity in design coordination, transport, craning, and local permitting. The site must also be able to support module delivery and assembly, which can be difficult on tight Los Angeles lots. A useful answer should explain that prefab is not automatically cheaper; it is a tradeoff between speed, coordination, and site feasibility. Searchers need help deciding whether their lot, schedule, and budget actually match modular construction or whether conventional stick-built construction is more practical.
acceptedAnswer.description: Prefabricated or modular methods can work for a fourplex, but success depends on site access, crane logistics, local approvals, and whether the design is standardized enough to benefit from factory production. Not every urban lot is a good fit.
